title: The Business of Health Care
description: This course introduces students to the business aspects of the health care delivery systems, including the philosophy of managed care, economics and financing of health care, administrative structures, and quality improvement. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Social and Behavioral Health
description: Overview of the impact of the social and behavioral sciences on health behavior issues. Key topics include examination of factors such as culture, race/ethnicity, gender, and socioeconomic status as they apply to family, community, organizational climate, etc., as well as social and behavioral science fundamentals employed to address past, present, and future public health concerns. 3 hours.

title: Biological Concepts for Public Health
description: Exploration of the major foundations of human disease from an ecological perspective that integrates population-centric approaches to the study of both infectious and genetically determined diseases. Specific topics include methods of infectious disease transmission, common disease risk factors and biological processes, and the impact of these topics on public health. 3 hours.

title: Epidemiology
description: Overview of principles of epidemiology with an emphasis on public health applications. Topics include examination of specific epidemiological tools used to help plan, monitor, and evaluate population health; consideration of methods for population health management; and understanding of factors influential to population health and the strategies that healthcare systems and organizations can implement for control of these factors. 3 hours.

title: Health Care and Public Health Policy
description: Introduction to health care services, including the characteristics and structure of the U.S. health care system and its comparison to other health systems. Key topics include examination of public health policy, laws, ethics, and economics; knowledge of key elements of the health care industry pertaining to medical care and public health; understanding of the interrelated roles of industry; and challenges facing state and national health care systems. 3 hours.

title: Evaluation Methods in Public Health
description: Discussion and application of processes surrounding public health evaluation, including issues of overall evaluation design, as well as methods and techniques used for conducting evaluations, communicating results, and ensuring that evaluation findings are used appropriately by intended users. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Program Planning and Evaluation for Public Health
description: Exploration of various practical skills used to effectively plan, implement, and manage programs that address public health problems in a range of settings. Key components include discussion of major concepts, theories, and methods in planning, implementing, and evaluating successful health promotion programs and events. 3 hours.

title: Advanced Topics in Public Health
description: A course devoted to special topics in public health not treated in other public health courses. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.

title: Advanced Topics in Public Health
description: A course devoted to special topics in public health not treated in other public health courses. 2 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.

title: Advanced Topics in Public Health
description: A course devoted to special topics in public health not treated in other public health courses. 3 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.

description: Investigations in area of current public health research with faculty guidance. Project plan must be presented to program director for approval. 1 hours. As needed.

description: Investigations in area of current public health research with faculty guidance. Project plan must be presented to program director for approval. 3 hours. As needed.

Repeatable for credit.

Repeatable for credit.

description: Student will conduct an experiential research project under the guidance of a faculty member. Student will meet weekly with their faculty research advisor and contribute to the design, implementation, analysis, and presentation of the research project. 3 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.

title: Public Health Internship
description: A structured field experience relevant to public health. Each internship is designed to provide a representative and meaningful learning experience for the participating student. Requires advanced planning and prior approval. 3 hours.

title: Physical Education Activity
description: Instruction and practice in sports and activities which contribute to present and future recreational needs, organic development, and fitness of the student. Instruction in the rules, strategies, social behaviors, and techniques of individual, dual, and team sports, folk, social, and square dancing, swimming and aquatics, conditioning and therapeutic activities, and other games and sports. No more than four hours allowed toward graduation. 1 hours. Laboratory two hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: Concepts of Physical Activity and Wellness
description: The course is designed primarily as an introductory course at the college level to provide the student with scientifically-based knowledge concerning physical fitness activities with concise and factual presentation with regard to the why, how, and what of exercise and physical activity for fitness and wellness. Lab sessions precede each outlined section. 1 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: Exercise and Fitness for the Older Adult - Land Exercise
description: An exercise class that may be taken by qualified older adults that offers chair, land, and walking exercise which is approved by the Arthritis Foundation. Open to Senior Wellness program participants only. 1 hours. As needed.

title: Exercise and Fitness for the Older Adult - Water Exercise
description: An exercise class that may be taken by qualified older adults that offers water exercise approved by the Arthritis Foundation. Open to Senior Wellness program participants only. 1 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: Exercise and Fitness for the Older Adult - Strength Training
description: An exercise class that may be taken by qualified older adults that offers strength and flexibility and cardiovascular training using strength machines. Open to Senior Wellness program participants only. 1 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Martial Arts
description: Students will be introduced to physical conditioning, stretching, and calisthenics (sit-ups, squats, lunges, push-ups, etc). 1 hours. As needed.

title: Aquacize
description: Wide variety of water exercises that provide for cardiovascular conditioning, toning, and strengthening of muscles. Performed in water deeper than seven feet. 1 hours. Fall, spring, as needed.

title: Cardioboxing
description: A challenging cardiovascular workout that combines boxing techniques and high-energy cross training. 1 hours. As needed.

title: Introduction to Philosophy and Ethics
description: This course presents a survey of the most basic issues in philosophy, with a special emphasis on ethical theory, ethical application, and professional ethics. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: World Religions
description: This course examines the role religion has played in the development of human society and common elements in various religious traditions. 3 hours. Spring, alternate years.

title: Death, Dying and World Religion
description: Explores and compares the cultural differences and similarities among societies going through the bereavement process. The course will also examine theological perspectives on death and dying, including how life and death are connected in the larger cosmological concepts of various world cultures. 3 hours. Fall, alternate years.

title: Philosophy of Religion
description: This course is designed to facilitate the student’s understanding of the process and content of religion. The student will have the opportunity to read about and to get involved in the investigation and debate about major issues within and about religion. 3 hours. Fall, alternate years.

title: Geography and World Religions
description: This course surveys the geography of the distribution, historical and cultural effects of world religions. It will provide students with opportunities for the study of the spatial variations in religious beliefs with and between countries, as well as how religion develops, spreads, and impacts a culture. This course also discusses materials related to major issues within religions and how they may be rooted in geographical factors. 3 hours. As needed. Same as GEOG 3413 and HIST 3413.

title: Women and Religion
description: Examines women’s religious practices and traditions in Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, and Hinduism. 3 hours. Spring, alternate years.

title: Physical Sciences Lab

title: Physical Sciences
description: The principles of elementary physics, chemistry, and earth science for the non-science major. 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Science for Middle School Teachers Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany PHSC 3003. 0 hours. As needed.

title: Science for Middle School Teachers
description: Designed to give the middle school teacher an awareness of the inter-relationship of the various sciences and the essential basic knowledge of new science innovations taught in the elementary school. Selection and organization of learning activities and materials for the teaching of science will also be emphasized. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Physics in Society Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany PHYS 1133. 1 hours. Laboratory two hours. Fall, spring.

title: Physics in Society
description: Study of fundamental concepts of physics for general education, with emphasis of learning physics principles on a need-to-know basis to address societal and technological issues. Designed for non-science majors. Does not count toward degree requirements in the College of Science and Engineering. 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: College Physics I Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany PHYS 2003. 1 hours. Laboratory three hours. Fall, summer.

title: College Physics I
description: Physics primarily for students in the health-related fields and industrial technology Topics include mechanics, thermodynamics, and acoustics 3 hours. Fall, summer.

title: Electrical Circuits I
description: The fundamental laws of circuit theory applied to resistive networks, network topology, mesh currents and node voltages, network theorems, one-terminal and two-terminal pair resistive networks. Also includes time response functions of R-L, R-C, and R-L-C circuits. 3 hours. Spring. Same as ENGR 2033.

title: College Physics II Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany PHYS 2103. 1 hours. Laboratory three hours. Spring.

title: College Physics II
description: A continuation of PHYS 2003. Topics include electricity, magnetism, optics, and modern physics. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Astronomy Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany PHYS 2133. 1 hours. Laboratory three hours. As needed.

title: Astronomy
description: This course will provide quantitative and qualitative conceptual understanding of space, solar system, and properties of stars, planets, galaxies, supernovae, cosmos, and the rest of the universe. Labs will be in form of telescope observations and computer simulation. Space will be limited. 3 hours. As needed.

title: University Physics I Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany PHYS 2203. 1 hours. Laboratory three hours. Fall.

title: University Physics I
description: An introduction to the principles of mechanics, wave motion, and thermal physics for science and engineering students. 3 hours. Fall.

title: University Physics II Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany PHYS 2213. 1 hours. Laboratory three hours. Spring.

title: University Physics II
description: A continuation of PHYS 2203. The fundamental principles of electromagnetic phenomena, including light. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Electromagnetism
description: A study of time independent and dependent electric and magnetic phenomena using differential and integral vector field methods. 3 hours. Fall, alternate years.

title: Modern Physics
description: This course is probably the most important physics course students will ever take. It is important because it is designed to expose students to various recent ideas that have changed our understanding of the physical world. The emphasis will be on the development of physics from the 1900s to the present day. We will closely study topics such as Einstein’s theory of special relativity, the structure of the atom, the basis of quantum theory and quantum mechanics, the Hydrogen atom, atomic and nuclear physics. If time permits, the course will also include the theory of elementary particles and some cosmology. 3 hours.

title: Advanced Physics Lab
description: Theory of instrument operation, procedure for instrument operation and theory of the experimental design. Experiments selected from modern physics and optics. 3 hours. Laboratory one hour. Fall, alternate years.

title: Optics
description: This course synthesizes the fundamental behavior and properties of light, interference and diffraction of light, geometric optics, Fermat and Huygens-Fresnel principles, optical interferometry, fiber optics, and lasers as time permits. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Analytical Mechanics
description: This course covers the principles of particular dynamics and rigid bodies. Topics include Newtonian mechanics, oscillating systems, conservation laws, rotations, and especially Lagrange’s equations and Hamilton’s principles. 3 hours. Fall, alternate years.

title: Quantum Mechanics
description: The course covers the basic ideas of quantum mechanics, which is the foundation and explanatory framework of much of modern physics. Solutions of Schrödinger’s equation in one dimension, formalism, and postulates of quantum mechanics and solutions of Schrödinger’s equation in three dimensions, in particular the hydrogen atom are all discussed. The students are expected to master problem-solving skills, learn about new mathematical techniques, and develop a conceptual understanding regarding the interplay between quantum mechanics and other areas of physics and the real world. 3 hours.

title: Principles of Horticulture
description: A study of the basic principles underlying the propagation, production, and handling of horticultural crops. 2 hours. Spring.

title: Soils Science Lab

title: Soils Science
description: A study of the origin, classification, physical properties, chemical properties, biological properties, and productivity of soils. Lecture two hours. 2 hours. Spring.

title: Elements of Forestry
description: General survey of the field of forestry including tree growth, pests, genetics, and management. Lecture two hours. 2 hours. Fall.

title: Forage Production
description: Principles of forage crop production for pasture, hay, and silage. Course will cover growth and development, production, nutritional quality, utilization, and grazing interactions by herbivores. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Greenhouse Management Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany PLSC 3032. 1 hours. Laboratory two hours. Fall.

title: Greenhouse Management
description: Modern greenhouse construction, climate control, and management of commercial and home greenhouses Identification, propagation, and study of major greenhouse plants. 2 hours. Fall.

description: Laboratory to accompany PLSC 3042. 1 hours. Laboratory two hours. Fall, alternate years.

title: Advanced Soils Science
description: A study of the chemical, biological, and physical properties of the soil as they influence the uptake and utilization of essential nutrients of plants. A look at the microorganisms and their biochemical processes in the soil. 2 hours. Fall, alternate years.

title: Entomology Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany PLSC 3073. 1 hours. Laboratory and field trips three hours. Fall, even years. Same as BIOL 3071.

title: Entomology
description: A study of the principal orders of insects with consideration of life cycles, economic importance, and methods of control. 3 hours. Fall, even years. Same as BIOL 3073.

title: Plant Physiology Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany PLSC 3083. 1 hours. Laboratory two hours. Spring, even years. Same as BIOL 3081.

title: Plant Physiology
description: A study of the basic physiological processes of plant growth and metabolism. 3 hours. Spring, even years. Same as BIOL 3083.

title: Weed Science Lab

title: Weed Science
description: A study of weeds as an economic pest occurring in both agronomic and non-agronomic situations including weed identification, ecology, growth and distribution, competition, and control. 2 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Introduction to Plant Pathology Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany PLSC 4022. 1 hours. Laboratory two hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Introduction to Plant Pathology
description: An introduction to the basic concepts of plant diseases, their impact on agriculture, and their control focusing on the four major areas of plant pathology: viruses, bacteria, fungi, and nematodes. 2 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Agronomic Production
description: Study of the production and management of economically important agronomic crops. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

description: An in-depth study of turfgrass selection, establishment, growth, and management in various managed turf areas. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Principles of Landscape Management
description: Establishing and maintaining plants in landscaped areas. 2 hours. Spring, odd years.

title: Special Problems in Plant Science
description: Individually designed for students who wish to conduct research in a specific area of plant science. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Introduction to Poultry Science Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany POSC 1003. 1 hours. Laboratory two hours. Fall.

title: Introduction to Poultry Science
description: Introduction to the principles of poultry sciences: broiler industry and egg industry, including nutrition, genetics, reproduction, growth, industry organization, processing, management and career opportunities. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Poultry Diseases and Health
description: A study of disease and health of poultry including epidemiology of bacterial, viral and fungal diseases and vaccination strategies. 3 hours. Fall.
prereq_text: ANSC 2002, ANSC 2001, POSC 1003, POSC 1001, and CHEM 1023 and CHEM 1021 or CHEM 1123 and CHEM 1121.

title: Poultry Nutrition
description: A study of intake, digestion and metabolism of domesticated poultry. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Egg and Meat Technology Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany POSC 3042. 1 hours. Laboratory two hours. Spring.

title: Egg and Meat Technology
description: Exploring the technology and practices for processing table eggs and poultry meat products. 2 hours. Spring.

title: Avian Anatomy and Physiology
description: An in-depth study of the anatomy and physiology of domesticated poultry, with emphasis on the skeletal, musculature, cardiovascular, reproduction, growth, respiration, and renal and liver functions. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Advanced Commercial Poultry Production Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany POSC 4142. 1 hours. Laboratory two hours. Spring.

title: Advanced Commercial Poultry Production
description: This course is intended to provide students with real world knowledge and experience regarding commercial poultry production systems, especially broiler chickens and broiler breeders. Students will learn how to manage their own broiler and breeder flocks and how to collect/analyze data. Current procedures and challenges found in the modern commercial poultry industry will be examined. 2 hours. Spring.

title: State and Local Government
description: A survey of government in the 50 states, with special application to Arkansas and with emphasis on intergovernmental relationships; problems of the executive, legislative, and judiciary; politics and elections; and local and metropolitan government. 3 hours. Spring, summer.

title: International Relations
description: A study of the global multi-state system’s origins and future prospects, and an analysis of techniques and forces governing international relationships. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.

title: Great Decisions
description: Analysis and discussion of contemporary problems in American foreign policy. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.

title: American Political Parties
description: The role and functions of political parties of the United States, with emphasis on party membership, organizations, nominations and elections, suffrage and voter behavior, interest-group politics, and relations with the executive and judiciary. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Criminal Law
description: An examination of the administration of criminal law in the investigation, prosecution, adjudication, and sentencing of criminals. 3 hours. Fall. Same as CRJU 3043.

title: Intro to Public Administration
description: A basic study of the methods, problems, and organization of public administration and of its relation to democratic government, including the problems of responsiveness and accountability. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: Administrative Law
description: An introduction to the methods of and conditions for policy analysis and project evaluation. This will include an examination of the strategies for effective policy development and analysis, as well as common means of project evaluation such as cost-benefit analysis and fair cost allocation schemes. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.

title: American Foreign Policy
description: A study of foreign policy’s constitutional basis in the Executive and Congress; the special role of public opinion in the American democratic system; a survey of America’s diplomatic history; and an analysis of contemporary foreign policy problems. 3 hours. Spring, even years. Same as HIST 3093.

title: Great Decisions
description: Analysis and discussion of contemporary problems in American foreign policy. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.

title: Western Thought
description: A study of the principal currents of thought in Western culture since 1800 with an emphasis on examination of the texts of selected philosophers. 3 hours. Spring. Same as HIST 3113.

title: Introduction to the Law
description: A general survey of law and the legal system of the United States. The course provides general coverage of all aspects of the law and legal system. 3 hours. Spring, odd years. Same as CRJU 3223.

title: Research Methods
description: An introduction to basic methods of research in history and political science, emphasizing computer-based quantitative analysis of historical and political phenomena 3 hours. Fall. Same as HIST 3133.

title: Modern South Asia
description: A survey of South Asia since the Mughal Empire with emphasis on imperialism, nationalism, independence, and modernization. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: Political Geography
description: A systematic and regional analysis of political units, including regions and cities; evaluation of geographic phenomena in the internal structure and external relations of the world’s countries. Attention is given to the problem areas of the world. 3 hours. Fall, even years. Same as GEOG 3193.

title: Immigration History Law
description: This course surveys the history and geography of American immigration from the era of colonization to the present, the process of immigration and adaptation of immigrants to life in the United States, and reaction to immigrants by American-born citizens. Course examines how immigrants fit within the larger framework of the American identity and help define what it means to be “American.” 3 hours. Fall.

title: Eastern Thought
description: A study of the principal currents of Eastern thought and religions, with an emphasis on examination of the texts of selected philosophers, schools, and belief systems. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Modern American Politics
description: A study of American Political development emphasizing the evolution of governing institutions, national parties, political culture, and interest groups since 1900. 3 hours. Fall, even years. Same as HIST 3243.

title: History and Politics of Modern China
description: An in-depth study of the political influences on Chinese history and the consequences of the decisions the nation made in the 19th and 20th centuries. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: History and Politics of Modern Japan
description: An in-depth study of the political influences on Japanese history and the consequences of the decisions the nation made in the 19th and 20th centuries. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: The American Presidency
description: A study of the American presidency, emphasizing the historical development of the office, the presidential selection process, the roles of the president, presidential-departmental-congressional relationships, and the growth of presidential powers and responsibilities. 3 hours. Same as HIST 3923.

title: History and Politics of the Middle East
description: A survey of Middle Eastern history and politics with an emphasis on the 19th and 20th centuries. 3 hours. As needed. Same as HIST 3933.

title: Legislative Processes
description: A study of the legislative process of city council, state legislature, and Congress; composition of membership, organization, and powers; and the relationship with other governmental bodies. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.

title: African American Politics
description: A study of the experience of African Americans in politics in the United States. The course includes analysis of the civil rights movement, as well as African American culture, political thought, and political participation on local, state, and national levels. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Comparative Public Policy
description: A study of the formation of public policy in developed and developing nations, alternative approaches to analyzing policy making, policy constraints, and selected public policies and decisions. 3 hours. As needed.

title: American Constitutional Law
description: A survey, using the case method, of principles, practices, and basic features of American constitutional law with emphasis on judicial review, the role of the Supreme Court, federalism, national powers, and individual rights. 3 hours. Spring, even years. Same as CRJU 4073.

title: Global Issues
description: Analysis of selected international issues such as population, resources, conflict, communication, development, and human values, from a global perspective, emphasizing transnational and interdependent relationships. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: History of Economic Thought
description: This course provides a survey of the development of economic theories. Particular emphasis is placed in developing an understanding of the relationships among economic thought, political science, contemporary philosophy, and sociological issues. 3 hours. Spring, even years. Same as ECON 4153 and SOC 4153.

title: Comparative Politics
description: A study of governing processes, policies, and contemporary political problems, comparing political systems around the world. 3 hours. Fall, alternate years.

title: International Law
description: This course is a general study of international law, with special emphasis on the discipline of public international law. 3 hours. Fall, odd years. Same as CRJU 4213.

title: Advanced Topics in Political Science
description: Advanced topics in political science as chosen by the faculty. 3 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.

title: Advanced Topics in Political Science
description: Advanced topics in political science as chosen by the faculty. 3 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.

title: Senior Paper Research
description: Undergraduate research and writing of a senior paper. This course provides a capstone research experience. Although supervised by an instructor, it is expected that a student enrolled in this course is able to work independently on a comprehensive research paper, requiring extensive investigation and producing original research. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Political Science Internship
description: This course provides a structured field experience in politics, government, and public policy. Students will be placed as interns with public agencies, political campaigns, or in private organizations interested in shaping public policy. Students will be required to complete assignments integrating scholarship with this practical experience. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: General Psychology
description: Introduces the fundamental concepts and basic factual content of psychology Students should gain a better understanding of their own behavior and that of other people. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: Educational Psychology
description: A survey course designed to meet the needs of prospective teachers by bringing an application of psychological principles of learning to the instructional settings. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Physiological and Comparative Psychology
description: A study of the comparative aspects of animal and human physiology and behavior, including the nervous system, sensory systems, endocrinology, and other topics. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Child Psychology
description: A study of the physical and mental growth of the child from infancy to adolescence. Special emphasis is placed on the social, emotional, motor development, interests, and imaginative activities of the child. Development of children in various cultural environments is explored. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Research Methods
description: A study of statistical methods, basic experimental procedures and designs, laboratory apparatus, and the treatment of experimental data. 3 hours. Fall, spring. Same as SOC 3153.

title: Statistics
description: Descriptive and elementary analytical statistics, their concepts, and their application. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer. Same as CRJU 3183, SOC 3183, and SWK 3183.

title: Advanced Topics for Individual Study
description: Individuals will study advanced topics in psychology and the social sciences as selected by faculty members. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.

title: Developmental Psychology

description: A course of comprehensive and intensive study of prescriptive Spanish grammar, including most aspects of Spanish grammar, such as phonetics, phonology, morphology, orthography, pragmatics, semantics, and syntax. The focus will be on syntax, as well as on those aspects of the language that students find most problematic. This course is taught in Spanish. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

The class is for upper-division Spanish credit. The readings will be in Spanish, and class discussions will be in English. 3 hours. As needed. Same as MCUL 4993.

title: Introduction to Public Speaking
description: Principles of effective speaking; emphasis on both transmission and reception of the communicative process; the speaking mechanism and delivery. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Advanced Public Speaking
description: Focus on enhanced preparation and delivery of major types of public addresses, as well as oral reports appropriate to group discussion and parliamentary procedure. Effective utilization of multi-media speech aids will be stressed. 3 hours. Spring, as needed.

title: Argumentation and Debate
description: Designed to develop advanced research techniques, critical thinking and analysis, and applied argumentation and persuasive skills. Course also includes practice for competitive debates and presentation. 3 hours. Fall, as needed.

title: Adapted Kinesiology
description: A study of individual education for typical and atypical students; basic materials, methods; and principles of a graded program of general class activities and special adaptive education and therapeutics of recreation for the disabled and handicapped. 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Special Education 101
description: This course is a concentrated study of individuals in P-12 grade levels with mild disabilities (learning disabilities, mild mental disabilities, behavior disorders) including theoretical, legal, and historical foundations specifically related to learner development, learning environments, curricular content knowledge, assessment, and instructional planning & strategies. This course meets the Special Education 101 requirements as outlined in the Arkansas Department of Education rules governing educator licensure. 3 hours.
other_requirements: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Inclusive Education
description: Emphasizes how to develop a positive learning environment that supports the inclusion of diverse learners and students with exceptionalities in mainstream settings. Candidates will study and apply co-teaching practices. 3 hours. Fall.
other_requirements: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Designing Assessments for General and Special Populations
description: Candidates will design and implement effective assessments for a variety of learners as well as provide focused and meaningful feedback. In addition, candidates will critically analyze data for purposes of accountability focused on improving individual and/or organizational performance. Emphasis will be placed on strategies for using assessment data to inform instructional planning for diverse learners. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
other_requirements: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Introduction to Special Education
description: This course provides an overview of the characteristics of persons with disabilities. Essential issues and theories relating to special education are emphasized. An additional emphasis is placed upon legal issues in the field of special education 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Foundations of Sustainability
description: Using a cross-disciplinary approach, this course introduces the various aspects of sustainability, including environmental, social, and economic dimensions of sustainability. This course will explore key knowledge areas of sustainability related to theories and evidence-based practice in several critical areas. 3 hours.

title: Special Topics in Sustainability
description: A study of current issues in the field of sustainability. Selected topics will be introduced from special readings and research. The course is designed to provide the student with in-depth knowledge in various areas of sustainability. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit with different course topics.

title: Special Topics in Sustainability
description: A study of current issues in the field of sustainability. Selected topics will be introduced from special readings and research. The course is designed to provide the student with in-depth knowledge in various areas of sustainability. 2 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit with different course topics.

title: Special Topics in Sustainability
description: A study of current issues in the field of sustainability. Selected topics will be introduced from special readings and research. The course is designed to provide the student with in-depth knowledge in various areas of sustainability. 3 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit with different course topics.

title: Sustainability Research and Applications
description: This capstone course for the sustainability minor allows students to engage in a project or research related to an area of sustainability of personal interest to them. Students will select a topic or project and then work individually or in teams to make an impact by gathering and sharing knowledge or engaging in community activities. 3 hours.
other_requirements: Admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: Admission to the College of Business.

title: Introduction to Social Work
description: Generalist social work practice with application in a variety of settings. Provides, in order: an introduction to social welfare and the development of social work as a profession; the knowledge, value, and skill base of social work; special populations and concerns in social work; and completion of 30 volunteer hours at an approved site. 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Community Service-Learning Experience
description: Designed to provide an overview of the practice of social work through a service project and traditional classroom-based methods. Offered to prospective social work majors. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Multiculturalism
description: An examination of the historical and contemporary perspectives surrounding the breadth of human experience. This class will emphasize the significance of recognizing and valuing each individual’s experiences, viewpoints, and perceptions. Students will explore a deeper awareness of themselves and their interactions with others, strengthening their ability to support and engage with people in meaningful ways. 3 hours. Fall, spring. Same as CRJU 3003, PSYC 3003, and SOC 3003.

title: Human Behavior in the Social Environment I
description: Theories and knowledge of human biological, psychological, and social processes as viewed from the micro- and mezzo-level perspectives with an emphasis on individual and family development. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Human Behavior in the Social Environment II
description: Theories and knowledge of human biological, psychological, and social processes as viewed from the mezzo- and macro-level perspectives with an emphasis on group and community development. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Rural Social Work
description: A focus on the understanding of the unique dynamics, needs and problems of the rural community. An examination of interventions and policy considerations in the practice of social work in rural settings. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Social Policy
description: An examination of the purpose, development, and implementation of social policy The relationships between social policy, ethics, and the goals of the social work profession are examined 3 hours. Fall.
coreq_text: SOC 3013 and SWK 2043 (can be taken as prerequisite or corequisite).

title: Social Work Practice I
description: An emphasis on basic social work skills, including knowledge and techniques in interviewing and establishing the helping relationship; understanding the application of the problem-solving process; and social work as practiced in an agency setting. This course is available to social work majors only. 3 hours. Spring.
prereq_text: BIOL 1043, BIOL 1041, PSYC 2003, SOC 2003, and SWK 3023.

title: Ethics
description: This course examines the methods used by the social workers when advocating for individuals, groups, and communities. Special attention is given to the role of ethics in advocacy. Both case and cause advocacy are considered. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Child Maltreatment Theory
description: A focus on the understanding of theories and research in child maltreatment and the identification of individual and systems risk of protective factors related to child maltreatment. An examination of the types of child maltreatment and their effects on the emotional, social, and intellectual development of the child. Instruction will include lecture and class discussion. Analysis of individual and systems factors in child maltreatment case studies is required. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Research Methods
description: A study of statistical methods, basic experimental procedures and designs, laboratory apparatus, and the treatment of experimental data. 3 hours. Fall, spring. Same as PSYC 3153 and SOC 3153.

title: Statistics
description: Descriptive and elementary analytical statistics, their concepts, and their application. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer. Same as CRJU 3183, PSYC 3183 and SOC 3183.

title: Crisis Intervention:
description: Designed to provide guidelines of intervention in order to promote self-growth and self-realization. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Domestic Violence
description: Examination of the causes, effects and legal aspects of domestic violence. Intervention techniques and prevention programs will also be studied. 3 hours. Summer. Same as CRJU 4003, PSYC 4003 and SOC 4003.

title: Critical Issues in Social Work
description: Introduces students to critical social work issues and to their impact upon individuals, families and communities. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Social Gerontology
description: An interdisciplinary course offering the study of the lifelong aging process, the changing social context of later life, societal response to the aged, and services available. 3 hours. Fall. Same as SOC 4073.
prereq_text: SOC 2003 or SWK 2043 and junior standing.

title: Family-Centered Child Welfare
description: Introduction to the concepts of family preservation, risk/safety assessment, and case management with emphasis on intervention strategies and services provided through child welfare agencies and related policy issues. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Grant Writing
description: This course is designed to provide the student with a comprehensive and in-depth understanding of the grant writing process. Emphasis will be placed upon how to secure federal, state, and private funds for elementary and secondary education programs, including counseling related programs. The course will address the basic components and supporting topics needed to prepare a grant application that can be successful in a funding competition. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Social Work Field Practicum Seminar I
description: This course will focus on issues directly involved in working with agency staff, individuals, families, groups, collaborations, teams, and other disciplines. Outside readings and internet searches focusing on the designated topics will be assigned weekly to prepare for the following week’s discussion.Experiential exercises designed to facilitate self-growth and awareness of students will focus on using various tools and techniques compatible with topics. An in-depth case presentation from the field will be required. 1 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Social Work Practice II
description: A study of the skills needed in assessment, planning, contracting, and evaluating in the generalist model. Each skill is related to the need for professional documentation along with ethical and legal considerations. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Senior Seminar
description: A weekly seminar to assist the senior student in transitioning from the student role to the professional role with an exploration of some of the possible difficulties. Issues such as obtaining employment, ethics, burnout, and establishing a support network will be covered. 1 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Child Psychopathology
description: This advanced level course focuses on the etiology, classification, and treatment of the child and adolescent psychological disorders that are most frequently encountered by professionals in mental health and educational settings. 3 hours. Spring. Same as PSYC 4163.

title: Advanced Topics in Social Work I
description: Varied topics of special interest to social work and the generalist model. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Advanced Topics in Social Work II
description: Varied topics of special interest to social work and the generalist model. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Social Work Field Practicum Seminar II
description: This course will focus on issues directly involved in working with agency staff, individuals, families, groups, collaborations, teams, and other disciplines. Outside readings and internet searches focusing on the designated topics will be assigned weekly to prepare for the following week’s discussion. Experiential exercises designed to facilitate self-growth and awareness of students will focus on using various tools and techniques compatible with topics. An in-depth case presentation from the field will be required. 1 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Social Work Practice III
description: This course is an examination of problems confronting geographic communities and the techniques social workers employ to address such problems. Various communities are considered in the practice content with an emphasis on the rural mezzo and macro practice. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Social Work Field Practicum I
description: Field study designed to provide students with an understanding of the practice of social work in varied settings and populations. This course requires placement in a public or private agency or institution and the completion of 240 hours of service to the agency or institution. Students will be given supervision as they synthesize knowledge, theory, and practice in a generalist practice model in direct social work within a social work setting. SWK 4844 should be taken during the semester immediately prior to SWK 4854. 4 hours. Fall, spring.
other_requirements: admission to Social Work Field Practicum
prereq_text: SWK 3123, SWK 3133, and admission to Social Work Field Practicum.

title: Social Work Field Practicum II
description: Field study designed to provide students with an understanding of the practice of social work in varied settings and populations. This course requires placement in a public or private agency or institution and the completion of 240 hours of service to the agency or institution. Students will be given supervision as they synthesize knowledge, theory, and practice in a generalist practice model in direct social work within a social work setting. SWK 4854 should be taken during the semester immediately following SWK 4844. 4 hours. Fall, spring.
other_requirements: admission to Social Work Field Practicum
prereq_text: SWK 4121, SWK 4844, and admission to Social Work Field Practicum.

title: Introduction to Education
description: This course is designed with the intent to prepare candidates to become prospective Arkansas teachers. Candidates in this course will study the foundations of American education, including important historical moments and acts, professional behavior, student needs and diversity, instructional methods including K-12 learners health awareness, communication strategies for all stakeholders, and reflective practices to support learning. Candidates will collaborate with an Arkansas teacher to actively participate in at least 25 hours of classroom observations and field experience opportunities. 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Creating Environments for Learning
description: This course will focus on increased proficiency in social-emotional learning practices and strategies for creating positive learning environments. Candidates will be provided with an understanding of the factors influencing individual and group behavior in school settings; methods of diagnosing school and classroom factors that may be eliciting the problem; and the options available for influencing student behaviors. Emphasizes classroom design including classroom procedures and expectations, organization of materials, and classroom space for optimum learner benefit. This course will require candidates to learn and practice strategies and techniques through authentic and interactive field experiences. 3 hours.
other_requirements: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: STEM Content for Teachers
description: Candidates will strengthen their subject matter knowledge in order to be better equipped for reaching the scientific pedagogy for K-6 students (including special needs and ESL learners). Candidates will utilize scientific inquiry along with the 5E model of teaching and the problem-based learning approach to enhance students’ critical thinking. Throughout the course, candidates will design instruction and utilize scientific technologies to effectively move student thinking toward meaningful understanding of the disciplinary core ideas; science and engineering practices; and crosscutting concepts within the realm of Earth, life, physical, space, and engineering science. 3 hours.
other_requirements: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Professional Learning I
description: The course will explore teaching practices based on student and candidate evaluation data during TEDU 4006. There will be a focus on responsive and collaborative communication in the classroom. 1 hours. Fall, spring.
other_requirements: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Residency I
description: The first residency semester requires experience in a classroom setting in the certification area sought under the supervision of University faculty. The candidate will be responsible for planning, implementing, and evaluating instruction in collaboration with the mentor teacher and in conjunction with the SAU site coordinator. Co-teaching is required. 6 hours. Fall, spring.
other_requirements: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Professional Learning II
description: The course will explore teaching practices based on student and candidate evaluation data during TEDU 4016. There will be a focus on professional growth and lifelong learning. 1 hours. Fall, spring.
other_requirements: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Residency II
description: The second residency semester requires experience in a classroom setting in the certification area sought under the supervision of University faculty. The candidate will be responsible for planning, implementing, and evaluating instruction in collaboration with the mentor teacher and in conjunction with the SAU site coordinator. Co-teaching is required. 6 hours. Fall, spring.
other_requirements: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program

title: Collaborative Practice
description: This course will focus on advancing student learning through peer collaboration by collecting and analyzing student work. 3 hours.
other_requirements: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Holistic Pedagogy
description: This course will examine education from a holistic lens to reveal the need for teaching all children in the current American schooling system. Candidates will focus on how instruction is strengthened by the integration of pedagogy, learning, and best practices for all learners. Candidates will question, analyze, and evaluate key issues and connections between schooling, community, society. Federal and state laws for all teachers including laws related to learners’ rights, teacher responsibilities, and adherence to state code of ethics will also be included. 3 hours.
other_requirements: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Assessment-Driven STEM Instruction
description: This course uses an inquiry-style method of teaching STEM concepts that will develop thinking and problem-solving skills. This allows pre-service teachers to build science understanding and skills for standards that require their students to be actively engaged in science and engineering practices. This course will require candidates to learn and practice strategies and techniques through authentic and interactive field experiences. 3 hours.
other_requirements: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Social Studies for Teachers
description: This course includes information about teaching and assessing social studies in elementary and middle school classrooms. The content will focus on United States history, government, citizenship, geography, anthropology, sociology, world history, and economics. This course will require candidates to learn and practice strategies and techniques through authentic and interactive field experiences. 3 hours.
other_requirements: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Assessment-Driven Social Studies Instruction
description: This course focuses on the methods of instruction for social studies by discussing learners and how to foster coherent, relevant, and inclusive learning environments. Candidates will practice data-driven planning and implement high quality instruction for students. Candidates will explore professional responsibilities through reflection, feedback, collaboration, and professional learning communities. This course will require candidates to learn and practice strategies and techniques through authentic and interactive field experiences. 3 hours.
other_requirements: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Ballet I
description: Introduction to classical ballet technique and terminology through barre and center floor work. Students will explore movement, alignment, and expression while developing an understanding of ballet’s artistic, cultural, and historical significance. The course emphasizes the connection between technical practice and broader human, social, and emotional perspectives in dance. 2 hours. Fall.

title: Ballet II
description: Continued study of classical ballet technique and terminology, building upon skills developed in Ballet I. Students refine alignment, strength, and movement quality while exploring more complex combinations, choreography, and expressive performance. The course deepens understanding of ballet’s artistic, cultural, and historical contexts and emphasizes the integration of technical skill with musicality and emotional expression. 2 hours. Spring.

title: Contemporary Dance I
description: An introduction to modern-based contemporary movement with elements of lyrical dance. Emphasis is placed on fluidity, musicality, creative expression, and the mind-body connection through technical exercises, floor work, improvisation, and across-the-floor progressions, supporting the development of strength, versatility, confidence, and individual artistic voice. 2 hours. Fall.

title: Contemporary Dance II
description: A continuation of modern-based contemporary movement with elements of lyrical dance. Emphasis is placed on balancing freedom and control while expanding technical foundations through advanced floor work, release technique, momentum-based movement, and complex across-the-floor combinations. Students further develop strength, flexibility, spatial awareness, musicality, and refined artistic expression. 2 hours. Spring.

title: Jazz Dance I
description: An introduction to the fundamentals of the Luigi and Giordano techniques of jazz dance, including warm-ups, basic technique, strength, flexibility, and mind-body connection, with an emphasis on musicality, style, and expressive performance. 2 hours. Fall.

title: Jazz Dance II
description: Expanding on the skills from Jazz Dance I, students will explore a variety of jazz styles, including commercial jazz and jazz funk, while developing choreography skills and expressive performance. 2 hours. Spring.

title: Musical Theatre Dance I
description: An introduction to original Broadway choreography, exploring the styles of Bob Fosse, Jerome Robbins, and Michael Bennett. Students will develop technical, collaborative, and performance skills essential for a career in musical theatre dance. 2 hours. Fall.

title: Musical Theatre Dance II
description: Expanding on skills from Musical Theatre Dance I, students will continue studying the styles and choreography of renowned Broadway choreographers, further developing the technical, collaborative, and performance skills essential for a career in musical theatre dance. 2 hours. Spring.

title: Production Run Crew
description: Hands-on participation in live theatre production, focused on theatre design and technology. Students will work directly with scenery, lighting, costumes, sound, media, and related equipment while supporting SAU Theatre’s annual season. Required for all SAU Theatre majors during their first two semesters of study. 0 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Acting I
description: An exploration of the discipline and art of acting through the fundamental principles and tools of performance. Students will engage with basic theatre terminology, script analysis, and character work through discovering and creating theatrical practices. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Freshman Seminar
description: This course provides an overview of the University community and resources, as well as an introduction to skills and strategies - such as time management, study, and test-taking strategies - for enhancing academic success. Required in the first regular semester of enrollment of all beginning freshmen and of all transfer students who have fewer than 24 semester credit hours. 2 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: Criminal Evidence and Procedures
description: A study of the legal and scientific principles involved in the acquisition, preservation, analysis, and presentation of physical evidence. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Criminal Law
description: An examination of the administration of criminal law in the investigation, prosecution, adjudication, and sentencing of criminals. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Ethics in Criminal Justice
description: This course will focus on ethical conduct and challenges faced by practitioners in various areas of the criminal justice system including courts, corrections, and policing Special attention will be given to recognizing and analyzing moral behavior, social moral norms, theories, and ethical behavior. Special attention will be given to identifying agency interventions designed to maintain high ethical standards in criminal justice. 3 hours. Spring.

title: American Government: National
description: A survey of the American National Government, including the Constitution; structure and operation of the Presidency, Congress, and Judiciary; federalism; civil liberties; and politics in action. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: Principles of Accounting
description: Introduction to the field of accounting, focusing on the fundamentals of financial accounting, creating financial statements and analyzing the financial position of publicly traded corporations using spreadsheets. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: Principles of Accounting II
description: Introduction to managerial accounting, including cost accounting, financial analysis for decision-making, and managerial reporting. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Survey of Accounting
description: Students will be introduced to principles of financial and managerial accounting, with emphasis on decision making. Ethical issues are also considered. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Intermediate Accounting I
description: Generally accepted accounting principles underlying the preparation of balance sheet, income statement, and retained earnings statement using spreadsheets. Problems and theory related to accounting for assets. 3 hours. Fall.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: ACCT 2003, ACCT 2113, and admission to the College of Business.

title: Managerial Accounting
description: Principles and practices of managerial accounting, with emphasis on cost management issues, including identification of cost activity bases, the measurement and reporting of cost information, and the use of cost information in decision making. 3 hours. Fall.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: ACCT 2003, ACCT 2113, and admission to the College of Business.

title: Individual Income Tax
description: Students will study federal income tax laws with an emphasis on the determination of federal income tax liability and tax planning for individuals. Students will be introduced to basic tax research techniques and reporting methods, and will gain experience in the ethical and accurate preparation of federal income tax returns using tax software programs. 3 hours. Spring.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: FIN 2003 and admission to the College of Business.

title: Accounting Information Systems
description: Study of theories and procedures of designing and implementing accounting information systems with emphasis on transaction cycles, internal controls, and the role of accounting data with an organization. The course provides hands-on experience with current accounting information system software. 3 hours. Spring. IS 3063.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: ACCT 2113, ACCT 2003, and admission to the College of Business.

title: VITA Experience
description: Provides volunteer experience preparing tax returns for low and moderate income residents through both classroom training and hands-on experience. 1 hours. Spring.
other_requirements: Admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: Admission to the College of Business.

title: Intermediate Accounting II
description: Problems and theory related to accounting for liabilities and equity, investments, revenue recognition, earnings per share, and cash flow statement. 3 hours. Spring.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: ACCT 3003 and admission to the College of Business.

title: Fraud Examination and Prevention
description: The course provides an introduction to the principles and ethics of fraud examination and prevention, including the fraud classification system, the nature of fraud, and understanding how to prevent and detect fraud in business entities. 3 hours. Summer.
other_requirements: Junior standing; admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: Junior standing and admission to the College of Business.

title: Business Internship in Accounting
description: A structured field experience relevant to accounting. Each internship is designed to provide a representative and meaningful learning experience for the participating student. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
other_requirements: Junior standing; approval of the Business Internship Committee
prereq_text: Junior standing and approval of the Business Internship Committee.

title: Auditing
description: Theory and practice of auditing as applied to financial statement audits, compliance audits, and operational audits. Also covers professional ethics for accountants and legal liability issues. 3 hours. Fall.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: ACCT 3103, ACCT 3063, and admission to the College of Business.

title: Accounting Data Analytics
description: Working with computerized accounting software, students will learn problem assessment, data preparation, data analysis, and data visualization through hands-on practice of real-world datasets. 3 hours. Fall.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: ACCT 3063, IS 3053, IS 3063, and admission to the College of Business.

title: Oil and Gas Accounting
description: An overview of the oil and gas industry and specialized financial accounting procedures associated with the industry, emphasis on accounting for exploration, development, production, depletion and amortization, joint operations, asset impairment and retirement obligation, includes reserve accounting/disclosure related to the above topics. 3 hours. As needed.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: ACCT 3003 and admission to the College of Business.

title: Advanced Financial Accounting I
description: Problems and theory related to advanced topics in financial accounting including pensions, leases, deferred income taxes, and financial statement analysis. 3 hours. Spring.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: ACCT 3103 and admission to the College of Business.

title: Advanced Financial Accounting II
description: Theory and practice of accounting for business combinations, consolidated financial statements, partnerships, estates and trusts, corporate liquidations, segment reporting, and international operations. 3 hours. As needed.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: ACCT 3103 and admission to the College of Business.

title: Governmental and Nonprofit Accounting
description: Generally accepted accounting principles for governmental and not-for-profit organizations, with emphasis on fund accounting and the preparation and analysis of financial reports using spreadsheets. 3 hours. Spring.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: ACCT 2113, ACCT 2003, and admission to the College of Business.

title: Advanced Taxation
description: A study of federal income tax laws with emphasis on the determination of federal income tax liability and tax planning for entities other than individuals. An introduction into state sales, use, and income tax laws. 3 hours. Fall.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: ACCT 3023 and admission to the College of Business.

title: CPA Review
description: Analysis and study of problems covered on the Certified Public Accountant examination related to financial accounting and reporting. 3 hours. As needed.
other_requirements: Admission to the College of Business; instructor permission
prereq_text: Admission to the College of Business and instructor permission.

title: Special Topics in Accounting

This course will be taught within the DCOVA (Define, Collect, Organize, Visualize, and Analyze) framework. Agribusiness and other agricultural data will be used to make data-driven decisions to make better business, management, and operations decisions in agriculture. 3 hours. Spring.

Fall.

description: This course will serve as the culminating course in a three-course agribusiness sequence following AGEC 3083 and AGEC 3093. Instruction focuses on investment analysis, evaluation of returns, and assessment of profitability to support informed, data-driven managerial decisions within an agribusiness context. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Agribusiness Finance
description: Introduction to concepts and methods in agricultural finance. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Agribusiness Problems and Policies
description: Study of current economic problems facing the agricultural producer and agri-businessman. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Risk Management in Agriculture
description: Introduction to the concepts of risk, risk analysis, risk management, and their application to the field of agriculture. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Introduction to Cultural Anthropology
description: An introduction to cultural anthropology, the study of culture and man in all times and all places. Major topics are the concept of culture itself, man as a culture bearing animal, and various aspects of culture such as language, social organization, economy, technology, and religion as they appear in primitive and modern societies. 3 hours. Spring. Same as SOC 1003.

title: Approaches to Archaeology
description: An introduction to physical anthropology and archaeology covering basic concepts in physical anthropology; the origins, evolution and racial development of man; basic concepts in archaeology; and the development of culture from the early Pleistocene up through the dawn of recorded history. 3 hours. As needed. Same as SOC 3043.

title: The North American Indian
description: The archaeology, ethnology, and history of North American Indians from the time of their arrival on this continent prior to 12,500 BC down to the present century. 3 hours. As needed. Same as HIST 3143 and SOC 3143.

title: Advanced Topics in Anthropology
