prereq_text: Admission to the College of Business.

title: Enterprise Risk Management
description: This course introduces the basic principles and concepts of enterprise risk management (ERM). Students will gain an understanding of how ERM integrates into an organization to protect and potentially enhance firm value through the optimal treatment of risk. Specific topics will include how to identify, analyze, and manage business loss exposures using insurance and non-insurance techniques. 3 hours. Fall.
other_requirements: Admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: Admission to the College of Business.

title: Financial Institutions and Markets
description: This course is a survey of topics including bank and non-bank financial institutions, money and capital markets, Federal Reserve System operations, financial crises, regulation of financial institutions and markets, and an introduction to the international financial system. Emphasis is on interlink of financial institutions, financial markets, and financial crises and regulation. 3 hours. Spring.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: ECON 2203, FIN 3003, and admission to the College of Business.

title: Entrepreneurial Finance
description: This course introduces the theories, knowledge, and financial tools and techniques an entrepreneur needs to start, build, and eventually harvest a successful venture. The course discusses important issues entrepreneurs face, including how and where to obtain financing, using business cash flow models, alternative solutions to commonly discovered problems, and positioning the early-stage company strategically. Students will be expected to conduct case studies on a variety of business types and present on a routine basis. 3 hours. Spring.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: FIN 3003 and admission to the College of Business.

title: Investments
description: This course is an introductory investment course that focuses on practical applications as well as analytical analyses of investment theories. It provides the basic knowledge about financial markets, valuation of investment tools, and different investment strategies. 3 hours. Spring.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: FIN 3003 and admission to the College of Business.

title: Fundamentals of Real Estate
description: This course explores the basic concepts of real estate ownership, management, and marketing. Additionally, it provides an inquiry into the legal requirements and instruments involved in real estate management. 3 hours. Fall.
other_requirements: Admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: Admission to the College of Business.

title: Business Internship in Finance
description: Junior standing and approval of Internship committee. A structured field experience relevant to the field of finance. Each internship is designed to provide a representative and meaningful learning experience for the participating student. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
other_requirements: junior standing; approval of the Business Internship Committee
prereq_text: FIN 3003, junior standing, and approval of the Business Internship Committee.

title: Advanced Financial Management
description: This course covers topics and issues in advanced corporate finance such as financial analysis, capital structure, dividend policy, agency policy, payout policy, and risk management through utilization of financial theory, tools, problems, and cases. 3 hours. Fall.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: Grade of C or higher in FIN 3003 and admission to the College of Business.

title: Life and Health Insurance
description: This course will cover business insurance needs as well as insurance needs for estate planning. It will focus on the analysis of life and health insurance and annuity products available in the individual market. 3 hours. Fall.
other_requirements: Admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: Admission to the College of Business.

title: Property and Casualty/Liability Insurance
description: This course will cover basic insurance principles, functions, and uses of property and casualty insurance for business; this includes commercial property, commercial auto, general liability, business income, inland marine, crime, and workers’ compensation. 3 hours. Spring.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: FIN 3013 and admission to the College of Business.

title: Retirement Planning and Employee Benefits
description: This course provides individuals with knowledge of both public and private retirement plans. The public plans include social security, Medicare, and Medicaid. The private plans include defined benefit and defined contribution plans and their regulatory provision. The specifics of various qualified plans and non-qualified deferred compensation plans are analyzed. 3 hours. Fall.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: FIN 3003 and admission to the College of Business.

title: Estate Planning and Taxation
description: A study of estate planning techniques and taxation. Specific topics include wills, will substitutes, trusts, forms of property ownership, charitable transfers, and estate and gift taxation, 3 hours. Spring.
other_requirements: Admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: Admission to the College of Business.

title: Advanced Financial Planning
description: A capstone course in financial planning. A comprehensive study of the various areas of financial planning with an emphasis on the integrated financial planning process. 3 hours. Spring.

title: International Finance
description: Topics to be covered in this course include theories of international trade and finance, foreign exchange rates, international movements of goods and services, international movements of capital and open market macroeconomic policies. 3 hours. As needed.

prereq_text: FIN 3003 and admission to the College of Business.

title: Senior Capstone
description: A senior level course aimed at furthering students’ knowledge of postgraduate opportunities. The objective of the course is to develop a body of work to be used in approaching possible jobs or graduate schools The content of the portfolio will depend on the student’s future goals. 2 hours. As needed.

title: Introduction to Leadership
description: This course focuses on introduction to the Army and critical thinking. It introduces candidates to the Army and the Profession of Arms. Students will examine the Army Profession and what it means to be a professional in the U.S. Army. The overall focus is on developing basic knowledge and comprehension of the Army Leadership Requirements Model while gaining complete understanding of the Officer Candidates School (OCS) program, its purpose in the Army, and its advantages for the student. Candidates also learn how resiliency and fitness supports their development as an Army leader. Includes a weekly two-hour laboratory facilitated and supervised by Cadre. 1 hours.

title: Basic Leadership Principles
description: This course introduces candidates to the personal challenges and competencies that are critical for effective leadership. Candidates learn the personal development of life skills such as critical thinking, time management, goal setting, and communication. Candidates learn the basics of the communications process and the importance for leaders to develop the essential skills to effectively communicate in the Army. Candidates will begin learning the basics of squad level tactics that will be reinforced during a weekly two-hour laboratory facilitated and supervised by Cadre. 1 hours.

title: Applied Leadership
description: This course focuses on leadership and decision making. The course adds depth to the candidate’s understanding of the Adaptability Army Learning Area. The outcomes are demonstrated through critical and creative thinking and the ability to apply Troop Leading Procedures (TLP) to explore innovative solutions to problems. The Army profession is also stressed through leadership forums and a leadership self-assessment. Includes a weekly two-hour laboratory facilitated and supervised by Cadre. 2 hours.

title: Army Doctrine and Team Development
description: This course focuses on Army doctrine and team development. The course begins the journey to understand and demonstrate competencies as they relate to Army doctrine. Army values, teamwork, and Warrior Ethos and their relationship to the Law of Land Warfare and philosophy of military service is also stressed. The ability to lead and follow is also covered through team building exercises at squad level. Includes a weekly two-hour laboratory facilitated and supervised by Cadre. 2 hours.

title: Training Management and Warfighting Functions
description: This course focuses on training management and warfighting functions. It is an academically challenging course where you will study, practice, and apply the fundamentals of training management and how the Army operates through the Warfighting functions. At the conclusion of this course, you will be capable of planning, preparing, and executing training for a squad conducting small unit tactics. Includes a weekly two-hour laboratory facilitated and supervised by Cadre. Successful completion of this course will help prepare you for OCS Phase 1 or Accelerated OCS, which you will attend in the summer at Fort McClellan, AL, or Camp Rapid, SD. 3 hours.

title: Applied Leadership in Small Unit Operations
description: This course focuses on applied leadership in small unit operations. It is an academically challenging course where you will study, practice, and apply the fundamentals of direct level leadership and small unit tactics at the platoon level. At the conclusion of this course, you will be capable of planning, coordinating, navigating, motivating, and leading a platoon in the execution of a mission. Includes a weekly two-hour laboratory facilitated and supervised by Cadre. Successful completion of this course will help prepare you for OCS Phase 1 or Accelerated OCS, which you will attend in the summer at Fort McClellan, AL, or Camp Rapid, SD. 3 hours.

title: The Army Officer
description: This course focuses on development of the Army Officer. It is an academically challenging course where you will develop knowledge, skills, and abilities to plan, resource, and assess training at the small unit level. You will also learn about Army programs that support counseling subordinates and evaluating performance, values and ethics, career planning, and legal responsibilities. At the conclusion of this course, you will be familiar with how to plan, prepare, execute, and continuously assess the conduct of training at the company or field grade officer level. Includes one laboratory per week supervised by OCS G.O.L.D. Cadre. 3 hours.

title: Company Grade Leadership
description: This is an academically challenging course where you will develop knowledge, skills, and abilities required for junior officers pertaining to the Army in Unified Land Operations and Company Grade Officer roles and responsibilities. This course includes reading assignments, homework assignments, small group assignments, briefings, case studies, practical exercises, a mid-term exam, and an Oral Practicum as the final exam. The Oral Practicum explores your knowledge of how you will be prepared for the Army Warfighting Challenges (AWFC) covered throughout the OCS G.O.L.D Advanced Course. Successful completion of this course will assist in preparing you for your BOLC B course and is a mandatory requirement for commissioning. Includes one laboratory per week overseeing MSL III lesson facilitation and supervised by OCS G.O.L.D Cadre. 3 hours.

title: Integrated Curriculum
description: This course synthesizes multiple disciplines to offer foundational training addressing the demands of 21st century classrooms. Candidates will gain the knowledge and exhibit the skills necessary to design and implement developmentally appropriate and effective teaching strategies dedicated to theory and practice. 3 hours. title: Physical Geology
description: Earth materials and general principles, including physical processes that shape the earth: weathering, erosion, volcanism, earthquakes, rock deformation, and mountain building. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Marine Geology
description: A study of the ocean basins, with special emphasis being placed on plate tectonics and structure of the ocean basins; geophysical processes responsible for the composition of the ocean basins; and marine sedimentation processes. Modern sedimentological and geophysical investigation techniques will be discussed. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Modern German I
description: An introductory course in contemporary German concentrating on speaking proficiency. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Modern German II
description: A continuation course in contemporary German concentrating on speaking proficiency. 3 hours. As needed.
needs_review: course OR non-course alternative

title: Promoting Academic Student Success (PASS)
description: This course provides students in academic distress a means to examine their transcript, study habits, and long-term academic goals through necessary academic advising and effective decision-making. Mandatory meetings, monitoring, class discussion, and assignments provide an opportunity to examine best practices for consistent and long term academic success. Credit earned in this course may not be applied to the total credit hours required for a degree. 1 hours. Fall, spring. Repeatable for credit.

title: Career Planning
description: Designed to help students consider the factors that will affect the career choices they make, to help them to start making some of those choices, and to facilitate some of the skills necessary to put their plans into action. 1 hours. As needed.

title: World History I
description: An introductory study of the nature and development of world civilizations to 1700. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: World History II
description: An introductory study of the evolution of modern civilizations since 1700. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: United States History I
description: A general survey of the history of the United States from the beginning of North American colonization through the Civil War and Reconstruction. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: United States History II
description: A general survey of the history of the United States from the end of Reconstruction to the present. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: Forum on Contemporary Affairs I
description: A multi-disciplinary study of contemporary issues through group discussions, films, and speakers. 1 hours. As needed.

title: Forum on Contemporary Affairs II
description: A multi-disciplinary study of contemporary issues through group discussions, films, and speakers. 1 hours. As needed.

title: American Foreign Policy
description: A study of foreign policy’s constitutional basis in the Executive Branch and Congress; the special role of public opinion in the American democratic system; a survey of America’s diplomatic history; and an analysis of contemporary foreign policy problems. 3 hours. Spring, even years. Same as PSCI 3093.

title: Western Thought
description: A study of the principal currents of thought in Western culture since 1800, with an emphasis on examination of the texts of selected philosophers. 3 hours. Spring. Same as PSCI 3113.

title: Russia and the Soviet Union
description: A survey of Russian and Soviet history with an emphasis on the 19th and 20th centuries. 3 hours. Fall, alternate years.

title: Research Methods
description: An introduction to basic methods of research in history and political science, emphasizing computer-based quantitative analysis of historical and political phenomena. 3 hours. Fall. Same as PSCI 3133.

title: The North American Indian
description: The archaeology, ethnology, and history of the North American Indians from the time of their arrival on this continent prior to 12,500 BCE to the present century. 3 hours. As needed. Same as ANTH 3143 and SOC 3143.

title: Modern South Asia
description: A survey of South Asia since the Mughal Empire with emphasis on imperialism, nationalism, independence, and modernization. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: African History
description: A study of Africa from its ancient history to modern day, including geography, slavery, colonization, trade, and religion. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Immigration History Law
description: This course surveys the history and geography of American immigration from the era of colonization to the present, the process of immigration and adaptation of immigrants to life in the United States, as well as reaction to immigrants by American born citizens Course examines how immigrants fit within the larger framework of the American identity and help define what it means to be “American ” 3 hours. Fall. Same as PSCI 3203.

title: Eastern Thought
description: A study of the principal currents of Eastern thought and religions, with an emphasis on examination of the text of selected philosophers, schools, and beliefs systems. 3 hours. Fall, even years. Same as PSCI 3213.

title: Modern American Politics
description: A study of American political development emphasizing the evolution of governing institutions, national parties, political culture, and interest groups since 1900. 3 hours. Fall, odd years. Same as PSCI 3243.

title: History and Politics of Modern China
description: An in-depth study of the political influences on Chinese history and the consequences of the decisions the nation made in the 19th and 20th centuries. 3 hours. Spring, odd years. Same as PSCI 3303.

title: History and Politics of Modern Japan
description: An in-depth study of the political influences on Japanese history and the consequences of the decisions the nation made in the 19th and 20th centuries. 3 hours. Fall, even years. Same as PSCI 3313.

title: Geography and World Religions
description: This course surveys the geography of the distribution, historical and cultural effects of world religions. It will provide students with opportunities for the study of the spatial variations in religious beliefs with and between countries, as well as how religion develops, spreads, and impacts a culture. This course also discusses materials related to major issues within religions and how they may be rooted in geographical factors. 3 hours. As needed. Same as GEOG 3413 and PHIL 3413.

title: World War II: Europe
description: This course examines the military, political, cultural, and social aspects of the Second World War in the European Theater. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: World War II: The Pacific
description: This course examines the military, political, cultural, and social aspects of the Second World War in the Pacific Theater. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.

title: The American Presidency
description: A study of the American presidency, emphasizing the historical development of the office, the presidential selection process, the roles of the president, presidential-departmental-congressional relationships, and the growth of presidential powers and responsibilities. 3 hours. As needed. Same as PSCI 3923.

title: History and Politics of the Middle East
description: A survey of Middle Eastern history with emphasis on the 19th and 20th centuries. 3 hours. Fall, odd years. Same as PSCI 3933.

title: Europe, 1815-1914
description: The history of Europe from the Congress of Vienna to the beginning of World War I, with special stress on reaction, nationalism, the industrial revolution, and imperialism. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Early Modern Europe
description: This course covers the most important political, economic, social, cultural, diplomatic, and intellectual developments in European (and world) history from 1500 to 1789. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Civil War and Reconstruction
description: A review of the sectional quarrel that led to secession; the military, diplomatic, and economic strategy of the opposing governments; the major campaigns on land and water; Presidential vs Congressional Reconstruction; and the economic, political, and social changes which accompanied the period. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.

title: History of Arkansas
description: A survey of the state’s history from pre-Columbian times to the present. The course will examine the critical developments which both encouraged and hindered the integration of Arkansas into the nation. Attention will be paid to the persistent political, economic, and social conditions as well as the role of significant figures who challenged the status quo. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: African American History
description: A study of the life, culture, and historical experience of African Americans within the broad context of American national development. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: American Social History Since 1900
description: A study of the American mind and character; popular culture including religion, movies, radio, and TV; and the social upheavals of the 1920s and 1960s. 3 hours. As needed.

title: World Travel Studies
description: This course offers an examination of the social, cultural, economic, political, and religious movements and the international relationships which have been operative and shaped world history. This course will provide students with an opportunity to learn about these topics through field trip study, living history, and museum visits. Students will learn how living history and museum visits can be utilized as academic experience. 3 hours. As needed.

title: American Social History Before 1900
description: A study of popular culture, social culture, social development, and patterns of thought from the colonial era through the 19th century. 3 hours. As needed.

title: World War II: The Home Front
description: This course examines the military, political, cultural, and social aspects of the Second World War on the Home Front. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Nazi Germany and the Holocaust
description: This course examines the most pertinent aspects of Nazi Germany and the Holocaust within the wider, world historical framework of ethnic cleansing and genocide. An emphasis will be put on the major debates and problems of interpretation. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: Europe Since 1914
description: A study of modern imperialism, the background of World War I, the rise of totalitarianism, World War II, and its aftermath. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: Recent United States History
description: A study of the Age of Roosevelt, World War II, undeclared wars in Korea and Vietnam, and American society from the Truman era to the Clinton administration. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Senior Paper Research
description: Undergraduate research and writing of a senior paper. This course provides a capstone research experience. Although supervised by an instructor, the student researcher is expected to work independently on a comprehensive research paper, requiring extensive investigation and producing original research. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Women in Europe
description: The study of the role of women in European history from the eighteenth century to the present. The course will examine women’s lives in the context of political, economic, and social changes. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Advanced Topics in World History
description: Advanced topics in history as chosen by the faculty. 3 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.

title: Advanced Topics in World History
description: Advanced topics in history as chosen by the faculty. 3 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.

title: Advanced Topics in United States History
description: Advanced topics in United States history as chosen by the faculty. 3 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.

title: Advanced Topics in United States History
description: Advanced topics in United States history as chosen by the faculty. 3 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.

title: History Internship
description: This course provides a structured field experience in the work of public history. Students will be placed as interns with appropriate private or public agencies (such as museums, state parks, or other programs) that have the mission of researching and presenting history for display to the public. 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Honors Seminar
description: Required of all students entering the Honors College within the first two semesters of enrollment. The Honors Seminar is an introduction to the academic experience, the Honors College, critical thinking, diversity issues, and other aspects of the academic life and the academic community. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Exploring Opportunities in Healthcare
description: This course introduces students to healthcare administration career options, part of one of the fastest-growing sectors in the US economy These positions include opportunities as hospital administrations, long-term care facility directors, medical practice managers, and occupations in the insurance industry and public health areas 3 hours. Fall.

title: Healthcare Informatics
description: Healthcare Informatics combines diverse disciplines such as information systems, social science, management science, behavioral science, communications, and healthcare to improve patient care quality and safety Students will learn to collect, store, analyze, and present health-related data in a digital format and improve health outcomes by applying informatics concepts, theories, and practices to real-world situations 3 hours. Spring.
other_requirements: Admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: Admission to the College of Business.

title: Internship in Healthcare Administration
description: A structured field experience relevant to Healthcare Administration. Each internship is designed to provide a representative and meaningful learning experience for the participating student. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.
other_requirements: Junior standing; approval of the Business Internship Committee
prereq_text: Junior standing and approval of the Business Internship Committee.

title: Human Resource Management in Healthcare
description: This course studies the essential role of human resources within healthcare organizations. It covers the principles, methods, and procedures related to the effective utilization of human resources in organizations. This course focuses on recruiting, selecting, training, and retaining a qualified healthcare workforce to solve tomorrow’s problems, be they technological, global, ethical, or motivational. 3 hours. Fall.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: MGMT 3023 and admission to the College of Business.

title: Challenges in Patient Care
description: This course focuses on the challenges of delivering quality patient care within the demands of the economic, social, legal, and political environment. Topics will include assessing patient care outcomes and relationships between management decision making and patient care in a variety of healthcare settings. 3 hours. Spring.
other_requirements: admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: HCAD 2003 and admission to the College of Business.

title: Healthcare Professional Capstone Project
description: A guided senior project in health care administration is to be completed under the supervision of an instructor. The project should include application of health care administration theories to a practice problem. 3 hours.
other_requirements: senior standing; admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: HCAD 3003, HCAD 4013, senior standing, and admission to the College of Business.

title: Methods of Teaching Individual and Dual Activities
description: This course is designed to develop knowledge, techniques, understanding, and skills in appropriate individual or dual sports and activities. Rules/officiating techniques; court/field/equipment requirements; and skills checklist with cues, history, and demonstrated proficiency are emphasized. A student-developed notebook is a requirement of the course. 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Methods of Teaching Team Activities
description: This course is designed to develop knowledge, techniques, understanding, and skills in appropriate team sports and activities. Rules/officiating techniques; court/field/equipment requirements; and skills checklist with cues, history, and demonstrated proficiency are emphasized. A student-developed notebook is a requirement of the course. 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Driver Training and Safety
description: Designed for students to learn to drive a car and develop good safety habits and attitudes, or for those who already know how to drive but would like to improve their skills. 1 hours. Summer, as needed.

title: Educational Field Experience I Lab
description: A supervised field experience which includes at least 25 hours of field experiences. Students are scheduled to participate in field experience with as many grade levels as possible (K-12) in as many different subject areas as possible in the partnering schools to which they are assigned. 0 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Introduction to Education
description: Introduction to Education is designed with the intent to prepare candidates to become prospective Arkansas teachers. Candidates in this course will study the foundations of American education including important historical moments and acts, professional behavior, student needs and diversity, instructional methods including K12 learners health awareness, communication strategies for all stakeholders, and reflective practices to support learning. Candidates will collaborate with an Arkansas teacher to actively participate in at least 25 hours of classroom observations and field experience opportunities. 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Officiating Baseball and Softball
description: Prepares students to officiate competitive baseball and softball games In-depth coverage of baseball and softball rules and the mechanics of officiating. Prepares the student to take examinations administered by rating boards. 1 hours. As needed.

title: Officiating Basketball
description: Prepares students to officiate competitive basketball In-depth coverage of basketball rules and the mechanics of officiating. Prepares students to take examinations administered by rating boards. 1 hours. As needed.

title: Officiating Football
description: Prepares students to officiate competitive football In-depth coverage of football rules and the mechanics of officiating. Prepares students to take examinations administered by rating boards. 1 hours. As needed.

title: Officiating Volleyball
description: Prepares students to officiate competitive volleyball In-depth coverage of volleyball rules and the mechanics of officiating. Prepares students to take examinations administered by rating boards. 1 hours. As needed.

title: Theory and Fundamentals of Basketball
description: Theory, strategy, and mechanics of coaching basketball, including the development of various systems of offensive and defensive play and basic supporting fundamentals. Attention to organization of the season, conditioning of players, and psychological factors peculiar to basketball as an educational medium. 2 hours. Fall, summer.

title: Theory and Fundamentals of Football
description: Theories, methods, and mechanics of coaching football, including consideration of fundamentals, rules, individual and team play, offensive and defensive formations, and game strategy. Discussion of practice sessions, squad organization, seasonal planning, conditioning of players, and education opportunities and values. 2 hours. Spring, summer.

title: Supervised Field Experience in HPSS for Elementary Schools
description: A planned, supervised field experience to include a minimum of 10 observational visits and 20 hours in the elementary level classroom or appropriate school setting. Students are scheduled to observe different levels and subjects found in the public school setting. The laboratory course is hybrid in nature and will require an online portfolio and an electronic journal. Emphasis will be placed on organizing content knowledge for student learning, creating an environment for student learning, teaching for student learning, and teacher professionalism. The portfolio/journal entries submitted in this course will comprise a significant part of the student’s grade for HPSS 3703. 1 hours. Fall.
other_requirements: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Supervised Field Experience in HPSS for Secondary and Middle Schools
description: A planned, supervised field experience to include a minimum of 10 observational visits and 20 hours in the secondary level classroom or appropriate school setting. Students are scheduled to observe different levels and subjects found in the public school setting. The laboratory course is hybrid in nature and will require an online portfolio and an electronic journal.Emphasis will be placed on organizing content knowledge for student learning, creating an environment for student learning, teaching for student learning, and teacher professionalism. other_requirements: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program

description: Observation and assisting in planning, teaching, and directing sports, dance, aquatics, conditioning, and recreational activities on community, school, and college levels. Preparation of analyses and critiques and carrying out of projected organizational plans followed by evaluation procedures under close supervision. 2 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Leadership in HPSS
description: A study of philosophy and fundamental principles of effective leadership in programs for private, public, and institutional settings. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Assessment-Driven Kinesiology for Elementary
description: This class prepares candidates to become effective elementary school physical educators. Candidates in the course will study physical education teaching styles, content development for lesson plans, research-based curricular models, and learn to use student performance data to modify teaching plans. In addition, candidates will collaborate with an Arkansas teacher to actively participate in at least 20 hours of elementary classroom observations and field experience opportunities. 3 hours. Fall.
other_requirements: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Assessment-Driven Kinesiology for Secondary
description: This class prepares candidates to become effective secondary school physical educators. Candidates in the course will study physical education teaching styles, content development for lesson plans, research-based curricular models, and learn to use student performance data to modify teaching plans. In addition, candidates will collaborate with an Arkansas teacher to actively participate in at least 20 hours of secondary classroom observations and field experience opportunities. 3 hours. Spring.
other_requirements: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Theory and Fundamentals of Baseball and Softball
description: Theories, strategy, mechanics, and methods of coaching baseball and teaching softball, including fundamentals of batting, fielding, base-running, throwing, and the playing of all positions. History, values, community opportunities, and service organization programs of baseball in American sport life is also discussed. 2 hours. Fall, summer.

title: Theory and Fundamentals of Track and Field
description: Theories, methods, and mechanics of coaching track and field events, including critical analysis of the techniques of sprinting, running, hurdling, jumping, and throwing. Emphasis on conditioning for competitive events, squad organization, workout schedules, off-season programs, and problems and actual experience in conducting track and field events. 2 hours. Spring.

title: Theory and Fundamentals of Tennis and Volleyball
description: Theories, methods, and mechanics of coaching tennis and volleyball, including consideration of fundamentals, rules, and individual and team play. The following elements will be covered in each sport: seasonal and daily practice plans, player conditioning considerations, team organizational procedures, psychological aspects, and offensive and defensive strategies. 2 hours. As needed.

title: Theory and Techniques of Rhythm Activities
description: Techniques, theories, and foundations of rhythm activities as media of self-expression in the development of the individual. Emphasis will be placed on the creative process and history of dance as a recreational form and instrument of cultural expression. Course elements include planning and organization of rhythm activities and materials in school kinesiology and sport science, as well as laboratory problems in folk, social, and contemporary dance. 2 hours. Spring.

title: Student Teaching Seminar
description: A seminar course to accompany elementary and secondary student teaching. The course includes the Program for Effective Teaching cycle, classroom management, and other professional topics. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
other_requirements: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

description: A planned, supervised student teaching experience for the college senior or student completing the teacher education/licensure program. Fall, spring.

description: A cumulative approach to making transitions from the academic setting to a professional career in HPSS. Portfolios, Praxis series, professional attitudes, appearance, mannerisms as well as job market skills will be stressed. 2 hours. Fall.

title: Advanced Driver Education and Traffic Safety II

title: Measurement and Evaluation of HPSS
description: A critical study of methods and uses of evaluation and measurement techniques in physical and health education and recreation. 3 hours. Spring, summer.

title: Personal and Community Health
description: A consideration of the various conditions and factors affecting individual and community health, designed to assist the student in formulating his own philosophy, attitudes, and understanding of behaviors necessary to establish healthful living practices. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: Human Anatomy and Physiology
description: A detailed study of the structure and functions of the human body with the emphasis on the skeletal, muscular, reproductive, and endocrine systems. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: First Aid & Safety/CPR
description: Course in advanced first aid, AED and CPR leading to a two-year certification from the American Red Cross. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: Techniques in the Prevention and Care of Athletic Injuries
description: The study and application of theory, principles, and techniques used in the prevention, care, and rehabilitation of athletic injuries. Introduction to programs in training and sports medicine. 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Kinesiology and Biomechanics
description: Analysis of the structural/functional aspects of human movement and the study of anatomic, mechanical, and neurophysiological factors influencing human motion. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: Adapted Kinesiology
description: A study of adapted kinesiology, a multi-disciplinary approach, consisting of a program of developmental activities, games, sports, rhythms, and aquatics suited to interests, capacities, and limitations of diverse students. Course includes collaboration activities, projects, legal issues, and requires a current background check. 3 hours. Fall, summer.

title: Pharmacology in Sports

description: A study of topological spaces, metric spaces, continuous functions, connectedness, separability, compactness, local compactness, and local connectedness. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.

title: Introduction to Complex Variables
description: An introductory course in complex variable theory with applications. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: Numerical Analysis
description: An introduction to the techniques of numerical analysis. Applications include finding roots of equations, numerical calculus, matrix methods for solving systems of linear equations, and the numerical solution of differential equations. Error control and algorithm complexity and convergence will be covered. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics
description: A study of the elementary theory of probability with statistical applications. The standard distributions will be applied to sampling theory, confidence intervals, and tests of hypotheses. Problem solving techniques and real-world applications will be stressed. 3 hours. Fall.

title: History of Mathematics
description: Presents the development of mathematics from antiquity to modern times. Explores how problem solving has spurred mathematical development. Examines the impact of culture on mathematics and the converse. Discusses mathematical literacy and proficiency from a historical perspective. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Data Science
description: Being a data scientist requires an integrated skill set spanning mathematics, statistics, machine learning, and data visualization. This course will introduce students to this rapidly growing field and equip them with the basic principles and tools. Students will learn concepts, techniques, and tools they need to deal with various aspects of data science, including statistical analysis, exploratory data analysis, predictive modeling, and data visualization. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Statistical Methods
description: This course will emphasize the basic principles and criteria for selecting the appropriate statistical techniques for data analysis, including descriptive statistics, discrete and continuous random variables, probability distributions, sampling distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing, simple and multiple regression, and statistical forecasting. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Special Topics in Mathematics
description: Special topics of interest, such as mathematical modeling, operations research, graph theory, dynamic systems, real analysis, etc. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Math for Teachers I
description: A study of numbers, operations, algebraic thinking, data, statics, and probability in a problem-solving approach for classroom teachers. 3 hours.

title: Math for Teachers II
description: A study of geometry and measurement through a problem-solving approach for classroom teachers. 3 hours.

title: Content Pedagogy in STEM
description: A content design course in which candidates will plan example learning units of study and equitable, culturally responsive opportunities for STEM students, based ontheir understanding of how students learn and develop mathematics and science knowledge, skills, and habits of mind. Candidates will make appropriate connections to math, science, and engineering practices and crosscutting concepts in their instructional planning content area. 3 hours.
other_requirements: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Math Connections
description: Candidates will be introduced to a wide variety of mathematics for teaching in middle and secondary schools. Concepts include number, trigonometry, and an introduction to calculus for teachers. 3 hours.

title: Assessment-Driven Math Instruction
description: This course focuses on critical issues of mathematics acquisition, assessment, and instruction. Attention will be given to understanding the interrelatedness of mathematics and other content areas, creating effective learning environments, planning and implementing lesson plans to meet the differentiated needs of a wide variety of learners, and assessing student learning in mathematics. This course will require candidates to learn and practice strategies and techniques through authentic and interactive field experiences. 3 hours.
other_requirements: Conditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program
prereq_text: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.

title: Introduction to Mass Communication
description: Development of communication media in American society, including newspapers, magazines, radio, television, and movies. Emphasis on social, political, and economic interaction of media and society. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Yearbook Practicum
description: Supervised work during one semester on the campus yearbook, The Mulerider. Experience in layout techniques, publishing work, and hands-on experience. 1 hours. As needed.

title: Yearbook Practicum
description: Supervised work during one semester on the campus yearbook, The Mulerider. Experience in layout techniques, publishing work, and hands-on experience. 1 hours. As needed.

title: Graphic Software Applications
description: Introduction to computer terminology, file management, network applications, and graphics applications in both PC and Mac environments. Emphasis on instruction using Adobe Photoshop and Adobe Illustrator software programs. 3 hours. Fall. Same as ART 2123.

title: Basic Digital Photography
description: The course will focus on the taking of photographs and the enhancement and printing of photographs from within a digital environment. Topics include terminology/technology, lighting, composition, depth of field, exposure, shutter speeds, lenses, digital file storage, and management and electronic. viewing Student must furnish their own digital camera, preferably with manual adjustments for focus, aperture and shutter. 3 hours. Fall, summer. Same as ART 2133.

title: Visual Communication
description: Presents the theories of perception, methods of analysis of visual media, the principles and strategies of visual communication emphasizing critical thinking about the role and function of media in society. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Directed Study I
description: This course will be individually designed to meet the needs of a student’s concentration in mass communication. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Yearbook Practicum
description: Supervised work during one semester on the campus yearbook, The Mulerider. Experience in layout techniques, publishing work, and hands-on experience. 1 hours. As needed.

title: Directed Study II
description: This course will be individually designed to meet the needs of a student’s concentration in mass communication. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Advanced Digital Photography
description: Open to all majors who desire concentrated exploration in digital photography to further develop their personal artistic growth both process-oriented and conceptual. The student will initiate a problem proposal in written form to receive approval from the supervising art faculty. Periodical progress reviews will be established. 3 hours. Studio six hours. Fall, alternate years. Same as ART 3363.

title: Media Law and Ethics
description: A study of national and state laws pertaining to mass media and of the ethical guidelines for media personnel, including ethical case studies in news media. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Yearbook Practicum
description: Supervised work during one semester on the campus yearbook, The Mulerider. Experience in layout techniques, publishing work, and hands-on experience. 1 hours. As needed.

title: Reporting and Writing for the Mass Media
description: Fundamentals for news reporting for print and electronic media. Topics include news values, journalism style/grammar, information gathering, and news writing. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Introduction to Media Production
description: This course is an introduction to the basic principles, procedures, and techniques of television production. Students are organized in teams and create various TV broadcasts. Students learn how to operate TV switchers, TV cameras, sound, and graphic equipment. The course covers the basic fundamentals of producing, scripting, directing, and editing for television. 3 hours.

title: Producing for Film
description: This course will cover the fundamentals of motion picture production including image composition, lighting, editing, and production planning. 3 hours.

title: Principles of Public Relations
description: Concept of public relations as management function in business, industry, education, and other institutions History, practice, and ethics of public relations. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Internet Communication
description: This course looks at the obvious and not so obvious ways that people, organizations, politicians, governments, and others utilize the Internet for communication and commerce. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.

title: Media and Politics
description: This course analyzes the decline of traditional media outlets, and the development of new media including networks, cable outlets, chatrooms, blogs, talk radio, websites. Discussions include how the media reports politics, how people get political information, and how politicians, political parties, and political organizations use the media to communicate, fundraise, and attempt to influence public opinion. The course will look at American and international politics and media outlets. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Producing Online Content
description: This course focuses on creating and curating professional content for diverse social media platforms, with the goal of engaging users, delivering messages, and building relationships. Video and motion graphics will be emphasized. 3 hours.

title: Trends in Modern Media
description: This course will examine current trends and changes in the media and how they will impact its future. Discussions will include the major changes and issues affecting print, broadcast, and cable media, as well as online media. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.

title: Screenwriting for Film
description: This course will introduce the student to the basics of screenwriting. It will involve the study of the three-act screenplay, format, plot, characterization, dialogue, theme, and scene dynamic. Study will include various short writing assignments, drafting of an outline, first draft, and revised draft of a 25-30 page screenplay. 3 hours.

title: Directing for Film
description: This course is an introduction to directing for the screen. Topics include casting, script analysis, working with actors, and storyboarding. Each student will direct and produce a short scene study. 3 hours.

title: Sports Production
description: This is a course discussing the different roles of the sportscast producer and show runners Particular emphasis will be put on exploring and discussing the difference between line, segment, coordinating, field, executive (show-runner), and supervising producers within sports broadcasts Students wear many television producer hats through the semester, and will explore those roles in relation to different scripted and non-scripted formats 3 hours.

title: Sports Broadcasting
description: This course teaches students to produce live sports broadcasts and sports studio shows. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: Directed Study in Mass Media I
description: This course will be individually designed to meet the needs of students concentrating in mass media. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.

title: Directed Study in Mass Media II
description: This course will be individually designed to meet the needs of students concentrating in mass media. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: Publicity, Media, and Campaigns
description: Concepts and case studies of public relations campaigns, and utilizing public media to achieve motivation of audiences. Materials and tools for publicity, planning, executing, and evaluating publicity campaigns are presented. Students enrolled are not allowed to receive financial compensation for work performed for campus media in order to meet course requirements. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.

title: International Public Relations
description: International public relations is a study of theories, advanced concepts, methods, principles and best practices of public relations as applied to international corporations, small businesses expanding into new markets, international non-profit organizations and local and foreign governments looking to attract business into an area. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: International Mass Media
description: This course looks at issues concerning global journalism, international mass media outlets, and the flow of information through traditional as well as online outlets. The course will also look at the influence of international media outlets, privatization and government control of media outlets, the impact of emerging media outlets in developing countries as well as the commercialization of media outlets. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Foreign Language Media in America
description: Focuses on the rise of foreign language (including Spanish, Arabic, Chinese, Korean, Russian and others) media and outlets in America. The course will look at print, satellite, cable, broadcast, and internet outlets marketed to immigrants, and originating in and out of America. The course will also look at how these emerging markets are used by corporations, politicians, and governments. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Editing for Film
description: This course will analyze and assemble dramatic scenes under a variety of conditions and narrative strategies. Editing theories, techniques and procedures, issues of continuity, effects, movement, and sound are examined as they relate to the fundamentals of cinematic montage and visual storytelling. 3 hours.

title: Cinematography
description: This course is an overview of the technologies and aesthetic principles of cinematography. The concepts covered will include digital formats, measurement and control of exposure, basic lens properties, camera support and movement, rules of composition, and the placement and control of light. Class sessions will consist of lectures, demonstrations, hands-on exercises and screenings of selected film clips which demonstrate specific cinematography techniques. 3 hours.

title: Writing for Sports
description: This course introduces the writing and reporting skills essential to sports journalism, broadcasting, and broadcast storytelling. Students will learn how news is gathered, evaluated, and distributed. They will also further explore the role that sports journalism and broadcasting play in the progressive media landscape. 3 hours.

title: Senior Research Project
description: To add to the graduate’s field of expertise, the student will write an extensive research paper. An oral quiz on the work will be required. 3 hours. Fall, spring; summer, as needed.

title: Mass Media Internship
description: Structured professional experience in a commercial or non-profit mass media area, such as newspaper, broadcast, cable, Internet, public relations or other mass media areas. Must be arranged in advance. 3 hours. Fall, spring; summer, as needed.
other_requirements: Senior standing; a minimum grade point average of 2.50; departmental permission
prereq_text: Senior standing, a minimum grade point average of 2.50, and departmental permission.

title: Hispanic Life and Culture
description: A course offering practical experiences of contemporary Spanish and Spanish-American life and culture. Presentations, films, documentaries, readings, discussions, demonstrations, and dramatizations of cultural interactions. Students will learn to converse about current issues, understand the cultural mores, and function effectively within Spanish and Spanish-American society. Readings and class discussions will be in English. Especially recommended for anyone interested in conducting international business. Does not apply to upper-level Spanish credits required for Spanish major or minor. 3 hours. As needed. Same as SPAN 4993.

title: Mechanical Engineering Capstone I
description: This course is the first part of a two-semester mechanical engineering capstone design course. Students will use theoretical and practical knowledge received in other courses of the mechanical engineering curriculum to provide practical solutions to design problems that resemble assignments that graduate engineers might receive upon employment. Students shall carry out design projects while satisfying multiple constraints, ethical practice, relevant industry codes of practice, and federal and state regulations. 2 hours.

title: Mechanical Engineering Capstone II
description: This course is the second part of a two-semester mechanical engineering capstone design course. Students will concentrate on prototyping their designs developed in MECH 4023 while completing three other assignments related to ethics, industry design codes, and the impact of technology on society. Students will also learn how to use their machine shop drawings in the prototyping process. 2 hours.

title: Business Communications
description: This course examines the principles of effective oral and written communications. The course provides practice in effective business writing, including letters, memos, resumes and reports, which are supported by proper research and documentation techniques. This course provides practice in effective oral presentations; and enhances interpersonal communications skills. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: Organizational Theory and Behavior
description: A study of organizational theory and human behavior in business organizations. An interdisciplinary analysis of relations of individuals and groups within the organization with special attention paid to management leadership responsibilities. Students are taught to consider the impact of dynamic forces like globalization and technology on the organization. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.
other_requirements: Admission to the College of Business
prereq_text: Admission to the College of Business.

title: Professional Communication Strategies
description: The course focuses on effective written and oral communication skills applicable in diverse professional settings The course includes practice writing and presenting professional reports that are used as tools of management The course addresses ethical decision-making and looks at how new technologies are changing the way people in business communicate 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: Leadership and Ethics
description: A study of philosophical models and practical techniques for leading an organization and for dealing with the types of ethical issues business leaders are likely to encounter in domestic and international environments. The course combines a study of relevant theory in each area with application-based exercises. 3 hours. Spring.
other_requirements: Admission to the College of Business

description: A structured field experience relevant to the field of management. Each internship is designed to provide a representative and meaningful learning experience for the participating student. 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Entrepreneurship
description: This course introduces foundational ideas and terms in entrepreneurship and innovation, with attention to developing students’ entrepreneurial mindset while cultivating the life skill of entrepreneurial thought and action Using lectures, cases, and practice-based activities students will be familiarized with the tools necessary to cultivate a business in a diverse, global environment Fall semester 3 hours.

title: Non-Profit Organizational Leadership
description: This course uses the PMD Pro Project Management for Development Professionals curriculum to provide nonprofit leaders the skills and experience to manage projects in the non-profit field. Students completing the course will understand how to deliver effective and transparent results that benefit communities and organizational stakeholders. Students that are interested in being a part of the ENACTUS team are encouraged to enroll in the course. The course culminates with the APMG Level 1 Project Management certification exam. 3 hours.

description: An introduction to the essentials of international business. Includes topics covering the nature of international business, international organizations and monetary systems, foreign environments, and special management and marketing considerations. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

description: The principles, methods, and procedures related to the effective utilization of human resources in organizations. Spring.

title: Operations Management
description: The management and analysis of operations and supply chain management, including such topics as productivity, quality management, sustainability, enterprise resource planning, inventory management, lean operations, and selected areas of operations research. Computer-based solutions will be used when applicable. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

description: A framework for diagnosis and analysis that enables the student to confront the problems and opportunities of complex business environments from the viewpoint of the policy makers. Technical, global, social, ethical, political, and legal aspects are all considered. A unique combination of text, readings, cases, and integrated simulation to develop the student’s ability to make decisions. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

title: Theatre Appreciation
description: A general overview of the art, history, and production techniques of theatre. 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Movement for Actors
description: An introduction to movement training for the stage, this course integrates anatomy, movement theory, and performance practice. Grounded in Laban Movement Analysis and Suzuki-based training, students will develop efficient, expressive movement and heightened body awareness. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Acting II
description: An exploration of the discipline and art of acting through discovery of how actors collaborate. Students will develop skills in imagination, communication, and collaboration with their fellow theatre practitioners and are introduced to the craft of creating a one-person show. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Voice for Actors
description: A foundational voice training course for performance, integrating anatomy, vocal theory, and embodied practice. Drawing from the work of Fitzmaurice, Knight-Thompson, Lessac, Linklater, and Rodenburg, students will develop efficient, expressive, and sustainable vocal production. Emphasis is placed on breath, resonance, articulation, clarity, and neutral speech to cultivate the voice as a responsive and expressive instrument. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Acting III
description: An exploration of the discipline and art of acting through theatrical movement practices and monologue work. Students will expand intellectual, physical, emotional, and ritual understanding of what personalization is and how it applies to the text of a play. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Acting IV
description: An exploration of the discipline and art of acting through audition preparation for theatre companies. Students will prepare self-tapes, broaden their career readiness, and investigate complex scene work. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Fundamentals of Design
description: A foundational theatre design course building on the concepts taught in Stagecraft. Students will explore the basics of all design specialties, including the tools, processes, and analysis methods used in professional practice, preparing them for advanced study in specific areas. 3 hours. Fall.

title: Costume Design
description: A practical introduction to costume design where students will develop skills in research, sketching, rendering, and fabric selection. Students will create and present design concepts, analyze construction techniques, and practice professional-level costume documentation and collaboration. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Improvisation
description: An introduction to improvisation focused on spontaneity, collaboration, and ensemble storytelling. Through structured exercises, games, and scene work, students will develop active listening, adaptability, and truthful responses in unscripted performance. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Summer Theatre Workshop
description: An in-depth study of theatre through the production of major plays for public presentation. 6 hours. Summer, as needed.

title: Summer Theatre Workshop

title: Stagecraft
description: An introduction to technical theatre where students gain hands-on experience with the fundamental skills of all production departments. Emphasis is placed on safety, basic tools, and collaborative work. 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Fundamentals of Acting
description: An introduction to practical acting skills for non-theatre majors. Students will develop confidence, imagination, concentration, and physical and vocal awareness through in-class exercises and scene work. This course will also introduce basic script and character analysis tools. 3 hours. Fall, spring.

title: Playwriting I
description: A practical introduction to playwriting where students will develop skills in crafting material for the stage. The course emphasizes dramatic structure, writing for performance, and understanding the technical limitations of theatrical production. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Acting for the Camera
description: An introduction to the skills and techniques specific to acting on camera. Students will explore professional terminology, on-camera practices, and practical exercises to build confidence and adaptability for film and digital performance. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: Accents and Dialects
description: A voice course where students will study and practice industry-standard accents and dialects using a systematic approach and the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA). Emphasis is placed on clarity, vocal flexibility, physical and emotional connection, and effective communication in performance. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Musical Theatre History
description: An overview of the development of musical theatre from the nineteenth century to present-day Broadway. Students examine key composers, lyricists, directors, choreographers, and performers, while analyzing historical, cultural, and performance elements to evaluate and compare musicals. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Musical Theatre Performance I
description: Intensive technique work in auditioning, acting, and musical theatre repertoire; focused on solos and scenes from Golden Age musical theatre material (pre-1965). Significant personal and group preparation is required outside of class. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Musical Theatre Performance II
description: Continued intensive technique work in auditioning, acting, and musical theatre repertoire; focused on solos and scenes from contemporary musical theatre (1965-present). Students will also explore the process of preparing a role, from character analysis to performance choices. Significant personal and group preparation is required outside of class. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.

title: Business of Acting
description: An introduction to acting as a business and approaches to becoming a working professional in the entertainment industry. Topics include headshots, resumes, new technologies, agents, unions, interviewing, auditioning, portfolio materials, and marketing. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Business of Design and Production
description: An introduction to professional marketing for theatre design and production students. Students learn to organize and present portfolio materials in digital, print, and media formats while exploring software tools to showcase their work effectively. 3 hours. Fall, even years

title: Special Topics in Theatre
description: Select areas of study in theatre not addressed by other theatre course offerings. May include technical, performance, history, literature, and criticism topics. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Hair and Makeup Design
description: An introduction to theatrical hair and makeup design. Students learn tools, products, and techniques for hair styling and wigs, as well as stage makeup application, including highlight and contour, aging, and injury effects. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Acting Styles I
description: This is an intensive course in classical theatre training focused on acting (including improvisation), movement (including movement theatre, clown, and historic dance), and voice. Texts might include those written by Aeschylus, Sophocles, Euripides, Aristophanes, Seneca, Plautus, and Terence, and moving into early modern with Calderόn, Sor Juana de la Cruz, Moliѐre, Racine, and Marivaux. 3 hours.

title: Acting Styles II
description: This course explores acting through the creation of ritual, social context/lessons, and transformational moments. The primary approach to the class involves the finding and rehearsing of scenes in the absurd and experimental genres, supplemented by readings, discussions, exercises, improvisations, and a monologue. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Theatre History I
description: Survey of the development of the physical theatre, presentation means and styles, origins and characteristics of tragedy and comedy, and representative plays from different periods of major playwrights from the origins of theatre to 1600. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Theatre History II
description: Survey of the development of the physical theatre, presentation means and styles, origins and characteristics of tragedy and comedy, and representative plays from different periods of major playwrights from 1600 to the present. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: Performance in Shakespeare
description: Approaches to acting the works of Shakespeare will be explored by various acting and vocal exercises. Two plays and sonnets will be explored for their action and character. Scansion of iambic pentameter, use of figures of speech, and use of verse and prose are just a few skills that will be developed. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: Creative Dramatics
description: An introduction to the process of creative and performing works for children. Students will learn about the structure and techniques of Theatre for Young Audience (TYA) plays, culminating in both in-class and out-of-class performances for live audiences. 3 hours. Fall, even years.

title: Script Analysis
description: A chronological and thematic study of dramatic literature through a wide range of plays, examined as literature intended for theatrical performance. Students will explore theatre movements, history, cultural context, structure, genre, and form as frameworks for playwrights’ work and scholarly interpretation. 3 hours. Spring.

title: Directed Study in Theatre I
description: Individually designed to meet needs of students concentrating in drama. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Directed Study in Theatre II
description: Individually designed to meet needs of students concentrating in drama. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Stage Management
description: An introduction to the skills needed for professional stage management. Students learn to notate cues and blocking, call performances, create rehearsal and tech schedules, and use other essential stage management tools. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: Survey of Black Theatre and Film
description: Students will explore the history of African American theatre from the early 19th century to the present. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Musical Theatre Performance III
description: Continued intensive technique work in auditioning, acting, and musical theatre repertoire. Focused on contemporary commercial music audition cuts for jukebox and pop-influenced musicals. Significant personal and group preparation is required outside of class. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Musical Theatre Performance IV
description: Continued intensive technique work in auditioning, acting, and musical theatre; focused on solos and scenes from the works of Stephen Sondheim. Students will also explore the process of preparing a role, from character analysis to performance choices. Significant personal and group preparation is required outside of class. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: Advanced Design Practicum I
description: Advanced study in theatre design where students will develop artistic and practical skills in their area of focus, emphasizing conceptual thinking and the collaborative design process. Students will create two projects using a Shakespeare play and a classical play. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Advanced Design Practicum II
description: Advanced study in theatre design where students will develop artistic and practical skills in their area of focus, emphasizing conceptual thinking and the collaborative design process. Students will create two projects using a contemporary American play and a musical. 3 hours. As needed.

title: Scenic Design
description: An in-depth examination of theatrical scenic design through a project-driven approach. Students will focus on the principles of design as applied to scenery, theatrical color theory, drafting, and modeling. 3 hours. Spring, even years.

title: Lighting and Sound Design
description: An in-depth examination of theatrical lighting and sound design using a project-driven approach. Instruction emphasizes color theory, equipment selection, light and sound plot development, integration with scenic structure, sound editing, and basic theatrical sound engineering. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.

title: Directing I
description: An introduction to the building blocks of the director’s process with emphasis on understanding and clarifying story and dramatic action. Students will engage in script analysis, exploration of symbolic imagery, blocking and stage composition, collaboration with actors and designers, and the creation of a director’s script. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

title: Devised Theatre
description: An introductory course in devised theatre, the process of theatre creation in a collaborative manner. The ensemble will create a theatrical piece, original or adapted, with the artists working as a collective. Students will be exposed to a variety of pedagogies in ensemble theatre-making, including adaptation and found text, viewpoints and composition, improvisation, and theater for social change. Students will study earlier works of devised theater as well as the history of theater as a tool for social comment and change. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.

title: Theatre Internship
description: Structured experience in a professional or university setting other than Southern Arkansas University in performance, production, stage management, costuming, or other areas of theatre. 3 hours. As needed.
